app.title: Sunspill: where the sun lands in your room
app.tagline: Draw a room, scrub the clock, see the sun cross the floor.
view.label: View
stage.hint: Drag to turn the room. Drag furniture and windows to move them.
stage.keys: Arrow keys turn the room in the 3D view. With a piece of furniture selected, the arrow keys move it in the plan view, or in 3D with Alt held, and the bracket keys turn it. With a window selected, left and right move it. Shift takes bigger steps.
live.item: {name}: {x} from the left wall, {y} from the bottom wall, turned {rot} degrees.
stage.ariaSun: The sun is {el} degrees up to the {dir} and {area} of floor is in direct sun.
stage.ariaNight: The sun is below the horizon.
dock.polarNight: The sun does not rise on this date here.
room.thicknessNote: Thick walls trim the sun that arrives at an angle, so the patch is smaller than the opening.
room.dial: Compass direction of the selected window
room.orientNote: Turn the dial to the direction you see when you stand at the window and look out. North is up.
room.compassSet: Window set to face {dir}. Phone compasses read magnetic north.
room.compassDenied: The compass is not available here.
win.title: Windows
win.name: Window {n}
win.none: No windows: the room stays dark.
win.acrossOn: A building blocks part of the sky
place.title: Where the room is
place.denied: Could not read your location. Search a city instead.
place.name: Name shown on pictures
place.zone: Time zone (name such as Asia/Taipei, or UTC+8)
place.zoneBad: That time zone is not known.
place.summary: Showing {date}. Change the date under the room.
place.note: Cities come from a list inside this page and your location stays in your browser. Address search and the map are in the guided setup, and each asks before it sends anything.
things.title: Furniture and plants
things.note: Drag a piece on the floor. Its top shows the sun that reaches it. Furniture does not cast shadows in this version.
things.max: That is the most pieces the room holds.
things.sunTop: Sun reaches the top for {t} on {date}
results.heatNote: Average hours of direct sun per day. Sample days: {n}.
results.legend: Hours of direct sun per day
tip.spot: {x} from the left, {y} from the bottom: {t}
results.westRule: Rule: on sample days from {from} to {to}, count the minutes after {after} when direct sun reaches the floor or a wall, and average them per day.
results.westLine: of direct sun inside per day after {after}
plant.title: Where a plant gets its light
plant.rule: Rule: the whole 30 cm footprint must fall in the chosen light level, using the period set under Sun hours map. Best spots first, at least 60 cm apart.
plant.none: No spot matches. Try another period or another light level.
plant.spot: {x} from the left, {y} from the bottom: {t} a day
share.title: Share this room
share.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the link and copy it by hand.
share.hideNote: Rounds the place to whole degrees and drops its name and the names of buildings in the link, the picture, the GIF and the file. Building shapes stay, because they decide the shade, so a very distinctive block could still hint at the place.
share.noSun: The sun does not rise on this date here.
share.gifNote: Made in this page, 540 pixels wide, 12 frames a second, silent.
share.importFailed: That file is not a Sunspill room.
card.floorNow: Floor in sun at this moment: {area}
card.assume: Clear sky, direct sun only. No reflections, no furniture shadows.
foot.privacy: Your room stays in this browser.
card.of: of direct sun inside, from {from} to {to}
compass.title: Phone compass
compass.hold: Hold the phone upright against the glass of the window, screen toward you, and keep it still.
compass.flatTip: Or lay the phone flat with its top edge pointing straight out through the window.
compass.unsteady: Hold still until the bar is full.
compass.none: No compass readings arrived. This browser or phone may not share its compass. Turn the room on the map, or type the direction instead.
compass.declination: The phone reads magnetic north. Sunspill corrects it to true north with the local declination of {d} (World Magnetic Model 2025).
map.off: The map pictures are off. You can still place and turn the room on a plain grid.
map.aria.pin: Map. Tap to drop a pin on the room. Drag to move, pinch to zoom.
map.aria.facing: Map. Drag the room to move it, turn it with two fingers or the round handle, pinch to zoom. North is up.
map.aria.surround: Map of the buildings and trees around the room. Tap one to select it.
net.body.search: Sunspill will send the text you type to nominatim.openstreetmap.org, a free service of the OpenStreetMap Foundation, and show the matches. The room itself is not sent.
net.body.tiles: The map is a set of small pictures loaded from tile.openstreetmap.org. Loading them tells that server which part of the world you are looking at, and your network address. The room is not sent.
net.body.buildings: Sunspill will send the position of the room, to about one metre, to an Overpass server (overpass-api.de, or overpass.openstreetmap.fr and overpass.private.coffee if that one is busy) and receive the outlines and heights of buildings within 200 metres.
net.note: Nothing is sent until you allow it, and you can switch each service off again from Online services at the bottom of the page. Without them Sunspill still works: type coordinates, use the built in city list and draw the buildings yourself.
trace.title: Trace a floor plan or photo
trace.pick: Choose a floor plan, a listing photo of the plan or a sketch. It is read in this browser and never uploaded.
trace.privacy: The picture stays on this device. Nothing is uploaded.
trace.badPicture: That file could not be read as a picture.
trace.scaleHelp: Tap two points whose real distance you know, for example the two ends of a wall that has its length printed. Drag a point to adjust it.
trace.cornersHelp: Tap two corners along one wall of the room, then any point on the opposite wall. Drag the dots to adjust.
trace.sizeRange: Rooms in Sunspill are between 1.5 and 20 metres a side. Check the scale.
trace.dragHint: Drag the dots until the outline sits on the walls.
trace.openHelp: Tap the two ends of each window or door along its wall. Skip this if the room already has the right windows.
trace.noWall: Those taps are not on a wall of the room.
wiz.finished: Setup finished. The room is saved in the link in the address bar.
wiz.place.intro: Type an address, a building or a town, or drop a pin on the map. The latitude, longitude and time zone fill in by themselves.
wiz.place.none: No address matched. Try fewer words, or drop a pin on the map.
wiz.place.noneOffline: No city in the built in list matched. Allow address search, or drop a pin on the map.
wiz.place.offlineOnly: Address search is off, so only the built in city list was used.
wiz.place.failed: The search did not work: {why}. You can drop a pin on the map instead.
wiz.place.pinned: Pin placed. Coordinates and time zone updated.
wiz.place.edit: Edit name, coordinates or time zone
wiz.place.privacy: Searching and the map ask OpenStreetMap servers, but only after you allow each one. The built in city list and your own coordinates need no connection.
wiz.room.intro: Pick the kind of room closest to yours, then correct the size. Sizes are typical for new apartments and suites in Taiwan.
wiz.room.floorNote: Count from the street: the ground floor is 1. If the lift shows 0 or G for the street level, add 1. The floor decides whether buildings across the street can block the sun.
wiz.room.more: More: wall thickness and floor height
wiz.room.traceNote: Use a floor plan or a listing photo of the plan. Tap a known distance for the scale, then the corners of the room. A room in Sunspill is one rectangle, so for an L shaped room trace the part the window lights.
wiz.room.traceButton: Trace a floor plan or photo
wiz.room.applied: Started from: {name}. Change the size to match your room.
wiz.room.traced: Room size and openings taken from the picture. Check the window heights in the next step.
wiz.win.intro: Set each window's place on its wall, size and sill height. Drag windows in the plan to move them. They snap to wall ends, the middle and each other.
wiz.win.roof: A roof or shade above (a balcony overhead, an awning)
wiz.win.snap: Measurements are real lengths. Change between metres and feet at the top of the page.
wiz.door.title: Doors
wiz.door.name: Door {n}
wiz.face.intro: Turn the room on the map until its outline fits the building, or read the direction with your phone held against the window. North is always up.
wiz.face.outlinesOn: {n} buildings are loaded. Drag the room over the one you live in. Turn it with two fingers or the round handle.
wiz.face.align: Line the window wall up with the building
wiz.face.aligned: Turned {n} degrees so the window wall follows a wall of the building. It faces {dir} now.
wiz.face.alignedAlready: The window wall already follows a wall of the building.
wiz.face.alignNote: Use this when the window sits in a main wall of your building. A bay or a wing that stands at an angle will not fit.
wiz.face.outlinesOff: Load outlines to line the room up with your building. This asks an OpenStreetMap server for the buildings within 200 metres.
wiz.face.northNote: Drag the room to move it. A phone compass is bent by metal and electronics by a few degrees, so compare it with the map.
wiz.map.partial: {n} of {total} buildings were kept: the ones that rise highest above your window. The rest rise less than {deg} degrees above it, so they only shade a sun lower than that. Load again after you change the floor number.
wiz.map.empty: OpenStreetMap has no buildings here. Add them by hand if there are any.
wiz.sur.intro: Buildings and trees that stand between the window and the sun. Load the buildings around you, then correct their heights, and add what is missing.
wiz.sur.status: {n} buildings and trees, {est} with a guessed height.
wiz.sur.effect: Direct sun inside on {date}: {a} with these, {b} without.
wiz.sur.estNote: Heights marked estimated come from the number of floors (3.2 m each) or a typical value for that kind of building, because OpenStreetMap has no height for it. Change them to what you see.
wiz.sur.bearing: Direction from the room (degrees, 0 is north)
wiz.sur.treeNote: A tree is treated as solid shade, so it shows the most shade it can cast. Leaf-off seasons are not modelled.
wiz.sur.balconyNote: Balconies and awnings of your own windows are set in the windows step.
wiz.things.intro: Add furniture and place it where it stands. The sun that lands on a piece is drawn on top of it.
wiz.things.pick: Tap a piece in the plan, or add one above. Drag to move it, drag the round handle to turn it.
wiz.things.keys: Keyboard: arrow keys move the selected piece, [ and ] turn it.
wiz.check.intro: Compare the model with the sun you really saw. Pick the date and time, then mark the corners of the sunlit patch on the floor, or lay a photo of the floor under the plan.
wiz.check.mark: Mark the patch on the floor
wiz.check.points: {n} points. Tap the corners of the sunlit patch one after another around its edge (at least 3).
wiz.check.pointsReady: {n} points. Add more or save this patch.
wiz.check.saved.title: Saved observations
wiz.check.none: Nothing to compare yet. Mark a patch.
wiz.check.overlap: overlap between the model and what you marked, over all observations
wiz.check.same: The model patch is where you marked it.
wiz.check.shift: The patch you marked sits {where} compared with the model.
wiz.check.dark: The model has no sun on the floor at that time, but you marked a patch. Check the date, the time and the direction.
wiz.check.fit: Fit the direction and windows to my marks
wiz.check.photo: Use a photo of the floor
wiz.check.accuracy: A match is not proof: marks from one hour can fit more than one room. Add marks at different hours for a stronger check. How accurate Sunspill is, and what it leaves out, is written in the accuracy notes.
wiz.photo.order: The plan is seen from above with the window wall at the top. Tap the four corners where the floor meets the walls, in this order.
wiz.photo.bad: Those corners do not make a room. Try again.
wiz.photo.ready: The photo now lies under the plan. Mark the sunlit patch on it.
wiz.fit.nothing: The model already agrees with your marks as well as it can. Nothing to change.
wiz.fit.noTurn: The direction stays as it is.
wiz.fit.turn: Turn the room by {deg} to face {to}.
wiz.fit.window: Move window {n} {slide} to the {side} and its sill {sill} {dir}.
wiz.fit.oneCheck: One observation can only tell the direction. Mark another hour to also fit the window.
wiz.fit.facingOnly: Only the direction changes: moving the window as well did not improve the overlap enough.
app.restored: Your last room was brought back from this browser. Start over in the Share tab.
wiz.check.byNumbers: Add a corner by typing its distances
wiz.sur.shadeNow: At {time}, {n} of these put their shadow on a window. They are outlined in orange on the map.
wiz.sur.shadeNone: At {time}, none of these puts a shadow on a window.
wiz.map.sunNote: The dotted line on the map points toward the sun at this time. Drag the clock to the time you remember the sun shining in, and see what it comes over.
app.linkAside: This room came from a link. Your own room is kept: open Share, then Bring back my earlier room.
app.buildingsCleared: The room moved to a new place, so the buildings loaded for the old spot were removed. Load them again in the surroundings step.
saved.title: Saved rooms
saved.name: Name for this room
saved.noName: Give the room a name first.
saved.full: Twelve rooms are saved. Delete one to save another.
saved.failed: This browser would not keep the room. Private browsing can do that.
saved.note: Kept in this browser only, and a name used again replaces that room. Opening one sets the room you had aside: Undo or Bring back my earlier room returns to it.
share.earlierBack: Your earlier room is back. Press the button again to return to this one.
wiz.leave.title: Leave the setup?
wiz.leave.body: The patch you were marking, or the photo of the floor, is not saved yet and will be lost.
wiz.sur.noSun: No direct sun reaches the floor on this day, even without these. Check which way the window faces, the roof or shade above it, and try another date.
wiz.check.night: At this time the sun is below the horizon, so there is no patch to compare. Set the time you saw the sun.
